title: Introduction to Financial Accounting
description: If you're an educational professional who are looking to progress into management and consultancy, or an educational planning or development role, this is the best degree for you.
body:
Provided by the KU Institute of Education, this programme is available by distance learning, allowing you to study flexibly while balancing work and personal lifes.

The MSc Finance (EG. Banking) deepens your understanding of banks and financial markets, and how they relate to performance. It will help you to advance your career in finance and policy.

title: Introduction to Managerial Accounting
description: This course provides graduate students with a comprehensive understanding of managerial accounting principles and their application in modern business decision-making environments.
body:
Students will explore cost behavior, budgeting, and performance evaluation techniques used by managers to plan and control business operations effectively.

The course emphasizes practical application through case studies and real-world scenarios, preparing students for leadership roles in financial management and strategic planning.

title: Intermediate Accounting I
description: An in-depth study of financial accounting theory and practice, covering the conceptual framework, income measurement, and asset valuation for undergraduate business students.
body:
This course builds upon foundational accounting knowledge to explore complex topics including revenue recognition, inventory valuation methods, and long-term asset accounting.

Students will develop proficiency in preparing and analyzing financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, equipping them for professional accounting careers.

title: Corporate Finance
description: A rigorous graduate-level exploration of corporate financial theory and practice, covering capital structure, valuation, and strategic financial decision-making in global markets.
body:
This seminar examines the financial decisions made by corporations, including investment policy, financing policy, and dividend policy, with emphasis on value creation for shareholders.

Participants will engage with cutting-edge research and real-world case studies from leading corporations, developing the analytical skills needed for senior finance roles in industry and consulting.

title: Marketing Principles
description: An introductory course covering the fundamental principles of marketing, consumer behavior, and the strategic frameworks used to develop effective marketing campaigns.
body:
Students will learn the core concepts of the marketing mix — product, price, place, and promotion — and how these elements are integrated to create compelling value propositions for target markets.

Through hands-on projects and industry case studies, students will develop practical skills in market research, brand strategy, and digital marketing that are immediately applicable in today's competitive business landscape.

title: Introduction to Computer Science
description: A foundational online course introducing students to computational thinking, programming fundamentals, and the core principles that underpin modern computer science.
body:
This course provides a broad introduction to computer science through hands-on programming exercises using Python, covering algorithms, data structures, and problem-solving strategies.

Delivered entirely online with interactive labs and weekly live sessions, the course is designed to be accessible to students with no prior programming experience while building a solid foundation for advanced study.

title: Strategic Management
description: An advanced graduate seminar examining the formulation and implementation of organizational strategy, competitive dynamics, and leadership in complex business environments.
body:
Students will analyze how organizations create and sustain competitive advantage through strategic positioning, resource allocation, and innovation, drawing on frameworks from leading strategy scholars.

The seminar format encourages deep engagement with real-world strategic challenges through executive case discussions, guest speakers from industry, and a capstone consulting project with a live client organization.

title: Microeconomics
description: A comprehensive introduction to microeconomic theory, exploring how individuals and firms make decisions and how markets coordinate economic activity in a modern economy.
body:
This course covers the fundamental tools of microeconomic analysis including supply and demand, elasticity, consumer theory, production and cost, and market structures from perfect competition to monopoly.

Students will apply economic reasoning to real-world policy questions and business decisions, developing the analytical framework needed for advanced study in economics, business, and public policy.
